notes: MariaDB 11.8 LTS. Replica configured by the official image (MARIADB_MASTER_HOST) using GTID slave_pos; MaxScale readwritesplit routes SELECTs to the replica and performs automatic failover (mariadbmon) when the primary dies.

ddl:
CREATE TABLE customers (
  id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
  country_code VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL,
  tier VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL,
  created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
  attrs JSON,
  PRIMARY KEY (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE categories (
  id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  parent_id INTEGER,
  name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  depth INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE products (
  id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  category_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sku VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
  description TEXT NOT NULL,
  price DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  attrs JSON,
  active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  FOREIGN KEY (category_id) REFERENCES categories (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(12) NOT NULL,
  ordered_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
  total_amount DECIMAL(14,2) NOT NULL,
  shipping_country VARCHAR(2) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE order_items (
  id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  qty INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  FOREIGN KEY (order_id) REFERENCES orders (id),
  FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE events (
  id BIGINT NOT NULL,
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  event_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  occurred_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
  payload JSON,
  value_num DECIMAL(12,4) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE inventory (
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  qty INTEGER NOT NULL,
  updated_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (product_id, warehouse_id)
) ENGINE=InnoDB

opt06_antijoin_forms.what: NOT EXISTS is the safest anti-join; NOT IN changes semantics with NULLs and may block hash anti-join plans

variants.name: left_join_is_null
variants.sql: SELECT p.id FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE oi.id IS NULL ORDER BY p.id

variants.name: not_exists
variants.sql: SELECT p.id FROM products p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi WHERE oi.product_id = p.id) ORDER BY p.id

variants.name: not_in
variants.note: NOT IN is NULL-unsafe and often slower
variants.sql: SELECT p.id FROM products p WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi) ORDER BY p.id

opt07_or_vs_union.title: OR across two different indexed columns vs UNION
opt07_or_vs_union.what: OR over different columns often forces a scan; UNION lets each branch use its own index (some optimizers do this automatically: bitmap OR / index merge)

variants.name: or_predicate
variants.sql: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ? OR id = ? ORDER BY id

variants.name: union_rewrite
variants.sql: SELECT id FROM (SELECT id FROM orders WHERE customer_id = ? UNION SELECT id FROM orders WHERE id = ?) u ORDER BY id

opt08_partial_index.title: Filtered/partial index for a selective status value
opt08_partial_index.what: partial indexes are tiny and fast for hot subsets (queues, pending rows)

variants.name: no_partial_index
variants.sql: SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-01 00:00:00' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00' ORDER BY ordered_at, id

variants.name: full_index_(status,ordered_at)
setup: CREATE INDEX ix_orders_status_ts ON orders (status, ordered_at)
variants.sql: SELECT id, customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND ordered_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-09-01 00:00:00' AND ordered_at < TIMESTAMP '2025-10-01 00:00:00' ORDER BY ordered_at, id

variants.name: partial_index_pending
variants.note: only PG / SQLite / SQL Server (filtered) / MSSQL

opt09_stats_refresh.title: Plan quality with stale vs fresh statistics (after bulk insert)
opt09_stats_refresh.what: row-count estimates drive join/scan choices; refresh statistics after bulk changes

variants.name: after_bulk_insert_no_analyze
variants.sql: SELECT c.country_code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events e JOIN customers c ON c.id = e.customer_id WHERE e.event_type = 'bench_stats' GROUP BY c.country_code ORDER BY c.country_code

variants.name: after_analyze
variants.sql: SELECT c.country_code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM events e JOIN customers c ON c.id = e.customer_id WHERE e.event_type = 'bench_stats' GROUP BY c.country_code ORDER BY c.country_code

opt10_batch_inserts.title: Insert batching: 1-row autocommit vs executemany(1000) vs multi-row VALUES(1000), one transaction
opt10_batch_inserts.what: round-trips and per-statement commits dominate small writes; batching amortises both
